candidates.source_name: Ephrem the Syrian / Commentary on Numbers
candidates.source_attribution: Ephrem the Syrian, Commentary on Numbers, on 19:1-22. NPNF Series 2, vol. 13. PD. Cf. Heb 9:13-14, 13:11-12.
candidates.draft_body:
Ephrem the Syrian Commentary on Numbers (c. 365 AD)

On the red heifer 'wherein is no blemish, and upon which never came yoke' (Num 19:2), Ephrem reads the unyoked, unblemished, wholly-burnt red heifer as the canonical Old-Testament type of Christ's atoning sacrifice — taken up explicitly by Hebrews 9:13-14 as the lesser-to-greater argument: if the ashes of a heifer sanctified the flesh, how much more shall the blood of Christ purge the conscience. The red colour anticipates the blood, the unyoked freedom anticipates Christ's voluntary submission, the outside-the-camp burning anticipates Calvary outside Jerusalem (Heb 13:11-12). Tewahedo eucharistic theology cites Num 19 + Heb 9 as canonical doubled-witness to Christ's once-for-all purifying sacrifice.
